text:
Sasha: Ran a full perf sweep on the 70B stack with TP=2 PP=2 DP=4 and saw a ~18% token throughput regression after the KV shard change. nvprof timeline attached (pasted below).

Kevin: Oof. Is the regression uniform across sequence lengths?

Sasha: Short seq (<=128) shows biggest hit. Long seqs regress too but less. It looks like all-reduce windows are blocking compute when we interleave KV syncs.

Maria: Can you paste the timeline + NVTX marks? also which kernel selection mode was used (auto vs tuned)?

Sasha: Using kernel_mode=auto; runtime picked fused-attn for most layers. Timeline snippet: 
```
NVTX: forward_layer_0 start
compute 12.3ms
KV_send shard_0->1 3.4ms (all-reduce kick)
compute 6.1ms
KV_recv sync 2.9ms
allreduce 5.8ms (blocking)
forward_layer_1 start
```
Notice heavy blocking during allreduce after KV send for each microbatch.

Jon: That pattern screams synchronous all-reduce per microbatch. We used to overlap with next-layer compute by chunking KV updates. Did the new sharding move KV updates to earlier in the pipeline?

Sasha: Yes — new KV sharding places each layer's KV on TP worker owning the layer partition. That reduced memory but we now do an all-reduce to consolidate hot keys for reroute and that happens inline.

Kevin: Two orthogonal levers: 1) move to async (non-blocking) all-reduce + wait only when KV needed, 2) change batching heuristics to increase microbatch size so compute > comm. For short seqs we can't increase tokens per request though.

Maria: Also check kernel selection: some fused kernels short-circuit compute earlier, exposing comm. If fused-attn reduces compute tail, the same comm becomes more prominent. Try forcing the older unfused kernel or add launch padding to smooth overlap.

Sasha: Ran a quick experiment forcing unfused attention on first 6 layers. Regression drops from 18% -> ~6% but CPU/GPU utilization increases. Not ideal.

Jon: Another approach: change KV shard placement to hybrid: TP-local for top layers (where KV hotness is high) and replicated DP for bottom layers (where comm dominates). That reduces cross-device all-reduce frequency.

Kevin: We could also amortize all-reduce across multiple microbatches using pipelined all-reduce (chunked ring) with background streams. Pseudocode: 
```
for microbatch in mbatches:
  start_forward(microbatch)
  if has_outgoing_kv:
    async_allreduce(kv_chunk)
  // do next layer compute while allreduce progresses
  wait_for_kv_if_needed(microbatch.layer+offset)
```
This requires kernel selection to avoid blocking CUDA stream syncs.

Sasha: Perf-bot trace shows our all-reduce launches on default stream sometimes force a sync with cuBLAS on stream 0. Perf-bot: 
```
perf-bot: rule match: allreduce_on_default_stream -> causes implicit sync with cuBLAS kernels on other streams.
perf-bot: suggested change: use ncclComm/NCCL_STREAM or cudaGraph-friendly streams to avoid syncs.
```

Maria: Good catch. If NCCL ops are on separate stream and we launch compute on another non-blocking stream, we can get overlap. Need to audit places where we call torch.distributed.all_reduce without specifying async handle.

Jon: There's also an opportunity to change KV cache behavior: instead of immediate global consolidation, do a stale-read model with local KV for N tokens and then reconcile. Many workloads tolerate slight KV staleness and it removes frequent all-reduces.

Kevin: Tradeoffs: staleness can affect deterministic outputs for exact-match workloads. We should add per-route config: kv_consistency: [strong, eventual] and let product teams pick. For strong, use sync all-reduce; for eventual, use local-first + background consolidation.

Sasha: I ran a background consolidation test: local-first for 16 tokens then async reconcile. Throughput improved ~22% on short seqs, and accuracy (nucleus BLEU for our eval set) dropped <0.4%. Promising.

Maria: Let's capture concrete action items:
- Audit allreduce calls to ensure not on default stream (Kevin)
- Add async allreduce path + tests for stream overlap (Jon)
- Prototype hybrid KV sharding (TP-local + DP replication for bottom layers) and measure memory vs comm (Sasha)
- Add per-route kv_consistency flag and experiment with 16-token staleness (Maria)

Jon: I'll take the async allreduce + integration test. I'll also add a microbench that runs short seqs (32/64/128) with perf counters to repro.

Kevin: I'll open a PR to default NCCL launches to a dedicated stream and add a guard for kernels that require default-stream sync (cudaGraph path).

Sasha: Putting my timeline + the quick background-consolidation script in the thread for anyone who wants to repro. TL;DR: comm/compute overlap is currently broken by default-stream allreduces + new KV placement ordering. We have multiple mitigations; hybrid placement + async allreduce + optional staleness look best.

Maria: Sounds good. @perf-bot, schedule a nightly perf run with TP=2 PP=2 DP=4 with staleness=16 and with default stream fix applied so we can compare baselines.

perf-bot: Scheduled nightly job: perf/70B/tp2-pp2-dp4/stale16 vs baseline. Results will land in #perf-results tomorrow morning. :robot_face:

Sasha: Thanks everyone — I'll update the design doc with the hybrid KV shard proposal and link the microbench numbers.
